references.text: Describes Mount Sinai as smoking and burning with fire when the Lord descended upon it, paralleling the description of the mountain burning with fire.

The people saw the thunder, the lightning flashes, and the mountain in smoke, and they feared and stood at a distance. They asked Moses to speak to them instead of God, similar to the action in this text.
Moses was called up along with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, corresponding to the tribal leaders and the elders who came to Moses.
Moses reminds the people that they heard a voice from out of the fire while the mountain burned, but they saw no form, only heard the voice.
The context explaining that the Lord spoke with them face to face on the mountain from out of the fire.
The people's fear of hearing the living God speak from out of the fire, continuing the theme from this text.
Hebrews refers to the Israelites coming to a mountain burning with fire, and to darkness and storm, and they asked that no more words be spoken to them.
